item.title: [ 45] I've been using split keyboards for roughly 3 years, and I'm considering going back to a regular one
item.description:
I first got a zsa moonlander, which was a big mistake, very bulky and the red thumb buttons made me angry, very ugly thing. Then I got the zsa voyager, on which I'm typing right now actually.

Typing on the voyager is overall a very good experience, butttttttt

I can't really explain it, but I'll try my best to do so.... somehow split keyboards just irritate me, maybe it's the way they look, they way they somehow make your desk look like a mess (especially the f'n cables! lord!) and also even though I am the only person looking at it, I feel as if it doesn't match with how I perceive myself. It looks like a contraption for the infirm, and the extremely nerdy. I just don't really see myself that way, although I'm big on ergonomics.

So I considered going back to a regular keyboard. A nice clean looking one without wires and without funky design. Something that you would see on the desk of a serious person, not gale bettinger.

Can anyone relate and has anyone gone through this process? Please let me know.

item.title: [ 74] Elon Musk Melts Down Over Perfectly Normal Questions in Wild New Interview
item.description:
https://gizmodo.com/elon-musk-economist-interview-2000790016

Elon Musk sat down with the editor-in-chief of the Economist for a taped interview that went live Thursday. The Tesla CEO has been avoiding normal journalists recently, even cancelling a planned interview with CNBC earlier this month. And it now seems pretty obvious why. Musk has a hard time answering normal questions about his often fascist and sometimes incoherent worldview.

The interview started cordially enough, with Economist editor Zanny Minton Beddoes asking Musk about his thoughts on the future of artificial intelligence. Musk said many things that he’s said before, including that AI will deliver an age of abundance, where “anyone can have anything they think of.”

Musk insisted that AI will exceed human intelligence in five years and that humans will no longer be in charge of the world in 10 years. Beddoes pressed Musk several times on what that means and how his companies will continue to exist. The billionaire rambled on and on in a way that didn’t really stand up to any scrutiny.

“If you have vast numbers of robots with vast amounts of digital intelligence, you have a sort of a quasi-infinite economy,” said Musk. “The future is going to be very, very different from the past. There’s no analogy or metaphor that I think illustrates the magnitude of change that we’re going to experience here.”

item.title: [300] The Official PowerPuffGirls discussion thread
item.description:
Blossom is best powerpuff. Bubbles is bipolar and Buttercup is a one note character that would look smarter if she stayed mute. In hindsight the movie would have done better if it was completely 90 minutes of action and was advertised with Buttercup kicking Satan in the face and giving him a nosebleed.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jw5oud8hTS0
One his softer reviews, I'm surprised he didn't mention the bus girl. He loves making fun of "Not" jokes.
He said everything that had to be said about the movie in 19 minutes albeit without shoving it in your face and without explaining it too much, just stating the obvious which autists ignore.

However I am swearing at him "What's with the monochrome space part? Is this a Swedish art movie?" Fuck you, I loved that part, but I'm not American so obviously I enjoyed artsie sensitive stuff. I wonder what he had to say about the Blind Archers Samurai Jack episode.
What did I have to say about PPG?
https://desuarchive.org/co/thread/154679056/#154691100


Also Doug Walker reviewed Speed Demon. I have not watched this review yet, I didn't even know it existed. However Speed Demon and RRB are the two episodes I have an issue with the ending, always had. And a PPG I do not take issue with and I consider it the finale is the one with the Professor's Dick friend. I always assign status quo shows a finale like how Samurai Jack had the infected Aku episode. I do that cause status quo shows don't have an ending even if the team behind it subconsciously assign one to a random episode. Dexter's Lab was a rarity among status quo shows.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p6z8xJUM9T8

As for the show itself ... it was a mixed bag that was always weaker than Dexter's Lab despite Craig having smarter ideas for attack moves than Genddy does that's obsessed with the human body language, but with PPG it's hard to do choreography so you have to rely on visual special effects attacks.

item.description:
Big mouth billy bass edition

previous >>109307783

READ THE (temp)WIKI! & help by contributing:
https://igwiki.lyci.de/wiki/Home_server

/hsg/ is about learning and expanding your horizons. Know all about NAS? Learn virtualization. Spun up some VMs? Learn about networking by standing up a OPNsense/PFsense box and configuring some VLANs. There's always more to learn and chances to grow. Think you’re god-tier already? Setup OpenStack and report back.

>What software should I run?
Install Gentoo. Or whatever flavor of *nix is best for the job or most comfy for you. Jellyfin/Emby/Plex to replace Netflix, Nextcloud to replace Googlel, Ampache/Navidrome to replace Spotify, the list goes on. Look at the awesome self-hosted list and ask.

>Why should I have a home server?
De-botnet your life. Learn something new. Serving applications to yourself, your family, and your frens feels good. Put your tech skills to good use for yourself and those close to you. Store their data with proper availability redundancy and backups and serve it back to them with a /comfy/ easy to use interface.

NEW YORK CITY - A morning commute in Lower Manhattan erupted into chaos after a suspect ignited a fire, set off commercial fireworks and brandished a pellet gun directly outside 26 Federal Plaza, a high-security complex that houses offices for the FBI, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and federal immigration courts.

The suspect, who was quickly taken into custody by federal security officers, has been identified by authorities as 43-year-old Andrew Arrabaca

Officials say Arrabaca, a former U.S. Army Patriot missile systems mechanic with ties to both Poughkeepsie and Harlem, arrived at the federal building with a variety of weapons and incendiary materials.

He was armed with six incendiary devices, commercial-grade fireworks, a bucket of suspected gasoline, two axes, a hammer, a machete, three knives and airsoft pellet guns/rifles.
Law enforcement officials characterized the suspect as an anti-government extremist driven by opposition to federal immigration enforcement.

"He came armed with bad intentions, looking to injure people and harm people," said James Barnacle, Assistant Director in Charge of the FBI’s New York Field Office.
